summary.text: An 8-year-old girl with a congenital single kidney and a history of epilepsy after encephalitis at age 2 presented to the emergency department with a 4-day history of fever and gross hematuria and periorbital edema. Laboratory findings showed profound proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia and mildly decreased kidney function, and she had no rash, arthralgia or alopecia. Family history included glomerulonephritis in a maternal uncle and recurrent hematuria in her mother and older sister.

Kidney biopsy showed IgAN (Oxford M1 S0 E1 T0) with a membranoproliferative pattern, and deflazacort was started, with mycophenolate mofetil added for persistent proteinuria. Two months after diagnosis she developed left upper extremity swelling with multiple axillary, subclavian and brachial vein thromboses on imaging, treated with intravenous heparin then 4 months of oral warfarin. SLE was suspected, but ANA and lupus anticoagulant were positive without meeting SLE or APS criteria.

Proteinuria remitted on deflazacort and MMF, and immunosuppressants were stopped at 6.5 and 7 months, leaving enalapril alone. Ten months later she had recurrent gross hematuria, leg purpura, epistaxis and acute kidney injury, with prolonged PT and aPTT, low complement, high anti-dsDNA, triple aPL positivity and factor II 41%. She fulfilled 2019 EULAR/ACR SLE criteria (score 22), and IgAN was reclassified as lupus nephritis with APS and LAHPS.

Methylprednisolone pulse, oral prednisolone and MMF produced remission; GC stopped after 2 years, proteinuria worsened 2 years later despite GC and higher MMF, and rituximab gave only an initial response. She now receives monthly cyclophosphamide with GC and MMF; nephrotic-range proteinuria persists with mildly reduced kidney function, but SLE markers normalized and no further thrombotic or bleeding events occurred at the last follow-up at age 15.

Kidney biopsy findings. (H, I) Electron microscopy shows electron-dense deposits (+), moderate mesangial deposits, moderate subendothelial deposits, and marked focal effacement of foot processes. article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the actual images are inspected in the separate visual target.
Anti-dsDNA at the last follow-up differs between text (<0.1 IU/mL) and Table 2 (<1.0 IU/mL); treated as a print-artefact ambiguity: the table cell is scored and the text value is review_only.
The case gives no calendar dates; times are durations from earlier events, table column labels, or ages.
Table 3 per-criterion points are recorded as observations of kind other; they are classification scores, not symptoms.
Discussion statements about other patients, cited literature and general LAHPS or SLE knowledge are not patient facts.
Table 1 platelet counts print K as a unit suffix; they stay as text without a converted number.
